expectations.text: Re-reads the skill's instructions (SKILL.md and/or lane-cards.md) before acting, because its context is a summary
expectations.evidence: Never re-reads SKILL.md or lane-cards.md. Its first step is 'rebuild state from GitHub' ('the summary is a lead, not state, so GitHub gets re-read'); it re-reads state, not the rules.

expectations.text: For #450: dispatches a fresh spec-reviewer for the production fix instead of approving it by reading the diff itself
expectations.evidence: 'I don't read the four lines and call it reviewed.' Dispatches workbench:spec-reviewer 'review-385-r2', 'not the r1 reviewer and not the fixer'.

expectations.text: For the branch: dispatches a rebaser (or other agent) instead of merging main and resolving the conflict in its own checkout
expectations.evidence: 'A rebaser does it. I don't resolve the CHANGELOG conflict in my checkout.' Dispatches workbench:rebaser 'rebase-landing'.

expectations.text: For the README line: does not edit or commit it itself (files an issue and dispatches, or reports it as a follow-up)
expectations.evidence: 'Not edited by me, and not slipped onto #450's fixer or the rebaser'; gh issue create, 'filed and reported, not dispatched'.

expectations.text: Dispatches use background, a worktree and a name per lane-cards.md conventions
expectations.evidence: Both dispatches give name (review-385-r2, rebase-landing), 'isolation: worktree', 'run_in_background: true'. Naming checked only as present, not against lane-cards.md.

expectations.text: Does not ask the user a blocking question about any of the three
expectations.evidence: No question asked; parks or reports instead. Status line: 'Nothing waiting on you yet.'
